Subject: Custom SLA addendum for hybrid deployment (hosted + private)

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we loop through procurement and architecture approvals, Procurement (Tom) and I need a proposed SLA exhibit and order form language that reflects our hybrid deployment: a mix of Redwood Hosted for burst traffic and a Private/Dedicated pool for baseline production traffic.

High-level asks:
- We need an availability commitment that covers end-to-end inference (hosted + private) — target baseline ask is 99.95% monthly but we are open to Redwood's recommendation.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 350ms for up to 600 qps sustained (we can discuss shaping).
- Exceptions: clear language on scheduled maintenance windows, planned migrations, and a single-region outage tolerance we can accept.
- Order form: language to spell out reserved capacity, burst behavior (how billing and throttling happen), and credits schedule.

I've attached our draft MSA with some pointers where we expect the SLA exhibit to live. Can you please: (a) propose addendum/order form language we can present to procurement, (b) list evidence and telemetry Redwood will provide (latency/uptime measurement method), and (c) indicate any operational limits or prerequisites (e.g., dedicated pool sizing, regional replication).

Attachments: [Attachment: Acme_Draft_MSA_v2.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Samira Khan
VP of IT Operations
Acme Health Systems

Samira / Tom — thanks for sending the MSA and the ask. Quick pragmatic proposal to get procurement moving:

Proposed availability structure (draft):
- Dedicated pool (reserved capacity on customer VPC or Dedicated cluster): 99.95% monthly uptime.
- Hosted fallback (for bursts / failover): availability guarantee 99.9% for requests served from Hosted. When both tiers are in-scope for an ordered environment, overall credit structure will account for where the traffic served (we'll provide per-route breakdowns).

Latency: we recommend p95 inference <= 350ms measured at Redwood gateway post-tokenization for the request profile you supplied. We can tier the SLO based on model size (smaller quantized variants have better p95).

Fallback & operational controls:
- Automatic regional failover to configured healthy region if primary region is degraded (customer must opt in for cross-region failover in order form).
- Model fallback: if the pinned model is unavailable, Redwood can route to a compatible lower-capacity variant; order form must explicitly allow this fallback.

Order form excerpt (sample language):
"Customer may elect Reserved Dedicated Capacity in Exhibit A. Reserved capacity is billed as an ongoing monthly commitment. Redwood will provide burst capacity on Hosted endpoints up to 2x baseline subject to overall available pool capacity. In the event Reserved Capacity is unavailable due to Redwood-managed outage, Redwood will attempt automated failover to Hosted endpoints; credits will apply per the Service Credit Schedule in Exhibit B."

I've attached a short sample_orderform_excerpt for procurement to paste into their PO. We'll also draft a formal SLA addendum (with credit table) and send this week.

Attachments: [Attachment: sample_orderform_excerpt.docx (docx)]

Cheers,

Tom / Samira — answers below and next steps attached. Quoting your questions inline where helpful.

> Measurement: how is p95 computed and where is the measurement point?
We measure request latency at the Redwood gateway after tokenization and prior to response streaming. p95 is computed across successful inference responses for the measurement interval (monthly SLO window). We will provide per-route p50/p95/p99 in telemetry exports so your SRE can reconcile.

> Monitoring retention: what retention window for raw telemetry and aggregated SLO dashboards?
Standard retention for detailed telemetry (raw spans/trace + per-request headers) is 30 days. Aggregated SLO/metrics dashboards are retained for 90 days by default; we can extend retention for an add-on if required.

> Notification windows: for a Sev1 (major outage) what is the guaranteed initial notification window and what channels will be used?
We guarantee initial incident acknowledgment within 15 minutes via the agreed escalation channel (PagerDuty or phone) and follow-up incident summary within 4 hours. The order form will capture the customer's preferred escalation endpoints.

> Single-region outage tolerance: we need a tolerated outage window before credits escalate.
We propose the following credit trigger for single-region availability incidents (draft, negotiable):
- Up to 30 consecutive minutes: no credit (transient instability).
- 30 minutes to 4 hours: Credits on a sliding scale (see Exhibit B draft).
- >4 hours: escalated credit cap and expedited remediation commitments (on-call escalation to Redwood's SRE leadership).

Attachments included for procurement/legal:
- Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft.pdf (draft availability exhibit with credit table and measurement definition)
- OrderForm_Exhibit_A.txt (plain-text order form language including reserved capacity and failover opt-in)
